metadata.title: Equally prepared for life? HOW 15-YEAR-OLD BOYS AND GIRLS PERFORM IN SCHOOL

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report describes the PISA 2006 assessment design and the construction of the science assessment framework, including the use of pencil-and-paper tasks (with computer-based additional questions in three countries) and student/background questionnaires. It also notes that, in a two-level regression context, students are Level 1 and schools are Level 2, and that “normalised final students weights as well as normalised replicates are used,” indicating complex survey weighting and replicate-based variance estimation in at least some analyses. However, the excerpt provided does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) or the full set of weighting procedures for all reported tables. For replication with PISA microdata, analysts should apply the standard PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the OECD PISA database and follow the report’s stated restriction rules (e.g., “This restriction applies to all analyses in PISA”).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The excerpt explicitly states that the dependent variables in the two-level regression are “the five plausible values in science,” implying plausible values were used and combined (consistent with PISA’s standard PV approach). However, the provided text does not document how missing questionnaire or background data were handled (e.g., complete-case deletion vs. imputation), which is a reporting gap for any analysis that conditions on questionnaire variables. Given PISA’s typical item nonresponse patterns, the absence of a documented missing-data strategy limits reproducibility of the reported gender/ESCS and related regression results.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report states that around 400,000 students participated in PISA 2006 across 57 participating countries and economies. It describes that students completed two hours of pencil-and-paper tasks, with additional computer-based questions in three countries, and that students also completed a questionnaire and principals (and in 16 countries, parents) completed questionnaires. The excerpt does not provide explicit inclusion/exclusion rules for an analytic subsample beyond a general note that “This restriction applies to all analyses in PISA,” and a note that for some analyses countries were restricted to those where students with an immigrant background represent at least 3% of the 15-year-old population. For the purposes of this extraction, the analytic sample is treated as the full available PISA 2006 student sample for the countries/economies referenced in the tables.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report documents the PISA 2006 science assessment framework and provides descriptive and comparative results on gender differences in science, reading, and mathematics among 15-year-olds. PISA 2006 involved about 400,000 students across 57 participating countries/economies, completing two hours of pencil-and-paper tasks; in three countries, some students received additional computer-based questions. The science domain used 37 science units (108 cognitive items) plus embedded attitudinal items, with items spanning multiple-choice and constructed-response formats and being organized around real-life science contexts (e.g., health, natural resources, environmental quality, hazards, frontiers). The report also links performance to student and school characteristics using questionnaire data and contextual indicators, including two-level regression structures (students nested in schools) and the use of the five plausible values in science as dependent variables. While the excerpt indicates complex survey weighting with normalized final student weights and normalized replicates, it does not specify missing-data handling for questionnaire variables in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is treated as a framework/technical documentation and descriptive reporting of PISA 2006 rather than an empirical machine-learning study. The provided excerpt contains no ML model training/evaluation pipeline, no predictive target-variable modeling, and no reported ML performance metrics. Therefore, main_findings and confounders_identified are left empty, and plausible values are handled as part of the PISA reporting framework (five plausible values in science) rather than as an ML-specific PV strategy.
